STATUTES

for

The association is founded at the founding general assembly Thursday the 30th of June 2022.


THE ASSOCIATION
SKAF - Association of Art Actors in Aarhus for Refugees


PURPOSE
The association's primary purpose is to make various art professional resources and infrastructures available to dissidents and refugees with a professional, visual artistic background in a broad sense, secondarily to create activities with visual artistic content for dissidents and refugees.


The association continuously develops, collects, and communicates offers of activities, materials, networks, residencies, etc., which are offered to dissidents and refugees who want to maintain artistic identity, be part of professional communities and get an artistic professional space.
Additionally, SKAF works to ensure that experiences with art and creative opportunities can become an offer in Aarhus Municipality to all refugees, including children.
Moreover, SKAF will reach out to other art forms and work to establish interdisciplinary artistic initiatives in Aarhus Municipality.
The association thereby supports artistic freedom, democracy and human rights by, through visual art, creating opportunities for refugees and dissidents arriving in the city. The association follows the guidelines for the Charter for Cultural Diversity - read more here: https://www.yumpu.com/da/document/view/20120874/charter-for-kulturel-mangfoldighed-pdf-center-for-kunst-

MEMBERS: Who can become a member of the association?
The association is open to professional art actors in Aarhus Municipality who have a special interest in the area and who wish to participate in the association's purpose. New members are approved continuously by the board. Members are admitted through a written request for membership, sent to the association's coordinator at the association’s email.


EXCLUSION OF MEMBERS:
Members of the association can be excluded if they do not live up to the association's purpose and values according to the statutes or otherwise create uncertainty about the association's work and values. Members will be excluded if a majority of the board agrees. The exclusion is made in writing from the board to the member.


GENERAL ASSEMBLY:
General Assembly is held once a year (physically or online) in March. Notice for the General Assembly and items for the General Assembly must be given at least four weeks before the assembly. The agenda is sent at least three weeks prior, and objections to the agenda must be sent no later than two weeks before the meeting. The agenda for the General Assembly is sent no later than two weeks before the General Assembly along with the accounts and proposals for any amendments to the statutes.


Those eligible to vote are divided according to how they are admitted in the association's membership groups – namely as institutions, artist communities, or as part of the group of individual actors. Each institution and each artist community has one vote (i.e., individual actors have a collective vote decided by a majority vote within the group of individual actors).


The agenda of the General Assembly shall contain the following points:
1) Election of chairperson
2) Presentation and approval of annual report by the chairperson
3) Presentation and approval of accounts by the treasurer
4) Possible amendments to the statutes
5) Presentation and discussion of the main lines for the association's activities in the coming year, as well as the budget for the coming fiscal year, including fixing next year's membership fee.
6) Election of board and deputies
7) Election of accountant (bookkeeper)
8) Information on new members – admitted continuously.
9) Any other business


Extraordinary General Assembly is convened with the same notice as the annual General Assembly. Notice is given when at least half of the board or half of the members require it with an indication of the agenda for the extraordinary General Assembly.


BOARD OF THE ASSOCIATION:
The association's board consists of 5 members, composed of members from each of the 3 voting groups (respectively the group of institutions, artist communities, or individual actors). The board appoints a chairperson, vice-chairperson, and treasurer at the first meeting after the General Assembly.
Besides the board, the association has two deputies who are invited to meetings and can participate if possible. Board members serve for 2 years and can be re-elected for two more years. 
New board members and deputies are appointed at the General Assembly. The coordinator cannot be chairperson of the board. The board decides its own rules of procedure.

At the founding General Assembly, two board members are exceptionally elected for only 1 years (to ensure dynamic turnover on the board).


FINANCE:
Membership fee is set at DKK 20 for individual memberships and DKK 200 for institutions and workshop communities. 
The annual accounts follow the calendar year and are approved at the General Assembly, where the treasurer presents the accounts (prepared by a bookkeeper elected at the General Assembly).
The annual accounts and accompanying comments are sent out together with the agenda for the General Assembly. The board signs the annual accounts.
Both chairperson and vice-chairperson are authorized signatories.


AMENDMENT OF STATUTES:
Approval of amendments to the statutes can take place at the General Assembly. Requests for amendments must be submitted no later than one month before the General Assembly. Amendments are carried out if 2/3 of the association's voting members agree.

DISSOLUTION OF THE ASSOCIATION:
The association dissolves if it cannot fulfil its purpose according to the statutes. The decision to dissolve the association is made at an extraordinary General Assembly. If 2/3 of the members agree, the association is dissolved. In the event of capital in the association after the final accounts, the capital is transferred to the Danish Refugee Council. Any surplus material is distributed to deserving and needy workshop communities among the members.
